note: mapping_basis=data_labels: the .do builds item = "P1002_" + line, where line is REG10A's L1002 (or REG10B's L1005 for ex-partner rows), a number-preserving rename of the source line code (core model s3 pattern 2). The data dictionary's value labels for L1002 tie lines 1..6 to the questionnaire's rows a..f ('la ignora o la trata con indiferencia?' = 1 ... 'piensa que le es infiel?' = 6), and L1005's labels give the same six contents in the same order in past tense, so the pooled codes denote the same behaviour in both registers, 6/6. POOLING (1002/1005): the .do stacks REG10B's 1005 (asked of women with no current partner, about the ex-husband/ex-partner/last partner, past tense: '¿Su ex esposo, ex pareja o última pareja que tuvo... la ignoraba o la trataba con indiferencia?' etc.) under the same P1002_<line> codes as REG10A's 1002 (current partner, present tense), keeping the current-partner answers for the one woman present in both registers. Live 3225 ids: 2402 answered 1002 wording, 823 answered 1005 wording (per item; REG10A 2403 women, REG10B 824, 1 in both). Per the batch_096 mascherini_2021_meddiet / batch_066 konerding precedent, item_text ships the 1002 current-partner wording (74% of respondents) and the 1005 variant is disclosed here and in public_note, not shipped as text. The 1005 rows as printed: b '… se enojaba cuando hablaba con otro hombre?', c '… trataba de impedir que vea a sus amigos/as?', d '… trataba de restringir o impedir que contacte o vea a sus familiares?' (no 'se'), e '… esperaba que le pidiera permiso cuando tiene una consulta médica?', f '… pensaba que le es infiel?'. The 1004G read-aloud framing differs from 1001G only in 'se casan, viven juntas o' for 'se casan o viven juntas o'; 1001G ships as instructions. RESP: the .do sets 9 (NR) to missing and recodes (6=1)(1=2), so source 1 Sí / 6 No becomes live 1 = No, 2 = Sí, and option_text is keyed to the LIVE codes (1 NO, 2 SÍ). Route 9: raw REG10A+REG10B counts (after dropping the both-register woman's REG10B rows) recoded equal live resp 1/2 in 12/12 cells: P1002_1 2716/509, P1002_2 2454/770, P1002_3 2927/297, P1002_4 3055/169, P1002_5 2950/274, P1002_6 2734/490; the unrecoded reading fails (P1002_1 raw 1/6 = 509/2716). Split REG10A-only / REG10B-only live 1/2: line1 2126/276 + 590/233, line2 1919/483 + 535/287, line3 2266/136 + 661/161, line4 2337/65 + 718/104, line5 2237/165 + 713/109, line6 2139/263 + 595/227. Dropped NR (9): REG10A 1 per line, REG10B 1/2/2/2/2/2 for lines 1-6. Live 19345 rows, 3225 ids, 3225 per item. validate_items.R --table-sets PASS (6 items, resp {1,2}). TEXT (text_source=study_materials): item_text = the questionnaire's shared stem '¿Su esposo, novio o pareja…' joined to each row's text with the row's own leading '…' and letter (a.-f.) dropped, which is how the manual instructs the question be read ('debe completarla con cada tema o ÍTEM'; example 'Su esposo, novio o pareja ¿La ignora o la trata a usted con indiferencia?'). Row d's line-wrap joined ('vea a / sus familiares?'). The dictionary's L1002 labels agree with the questionnaire rows verbatim. instructions = 1001G's read-aloud text without the interviewer direction 'ENCUESTADORA, léale lo siguiente a la entrevistada:' and the quotation marks; the questionnaire's line-break hyphen 'pare-ja' joined. option_text = the questionnaire's column headers verbatim (SÍ / NO; the dictionary spells them Sí / No); no row for NR 9. The 1003/1006 12-month follow-up is not in this table. Single section_id, no section_prompt. language=Spanish; translation_source=machine_translation: INE publishes the ENSIMUP in Spanish only; all English produced by IRW ('amigos/as' rendered 'friends', 'familiares' 'relatives', 'consulta médica' 'medical appointment'). Issues-page entry owed once live. public_note: The English wording for this table was produced by IRW, not by INE Paraguay, which publishes the ENSIMUP 2021 in Spanish only; the item text is the current-partner question (1002, present tense), but the item codes also carry the answers of women without a current partner, who were asked the same six questions in the past tense about their ex-husband, ex-partner or last partner (question 1005, about a quarter of respondents); and the response codes were reversed in processing so that 1 = No and 2 = Sí (yes), unlike the questionnaire's 1 = Sí, 6 = No.
